subtitle: Short domains that are actually free
description:
Type a name and Domains tries the shorter versions of it: clipped forms, sound-alikes, initials, a dropped vowel, AI ideas and domain hacks. From Zacharia it makes zach, zack, zak and zchr; from flicker, flickr.

Each label meets the extensions you pick: short ones like .io, .so and .sh, every two- or three-letter extension, or your own from Namecheap's 571 with their prices. Domains checks them all live, shortest first. Every name gets a card whose extensions wait, then settle to free or taken, and the shortest free ones gather as tiles at the top.

One switch hides what's taken, another hides premium names, and a price limit does the rest. Tap a name for its first-year and renewal prices, who holds it if it's taken, and a link to register it. Star the ones you like; sign in to keep them on every device.

Lookups go through adapters: a Namecheap adapter today, with the registries' own RDAP as a fallback, so another service can take their place.
whatsNew: First release: shorter names, sound-alikes and AI ideas checked live across short extensions, shortest first, with a Namecheap adapter, an RDAP fallback, filters for free, premium and price, and saved names.
